name: LED Blinking
summary: The hello-world of embedded systems: toggle an LED with a delay, then with a hardware timer.
hardware: Any development board (Arduino, STM32 Nucleo, ESP32, ...)
software: Vendor IDE, Arduino IDE or PlatformIO
outcomes: Replace a blocking delay with a timer

name: Push Button Interface
summary: Read a button reliably: pull-up/pull-down, debouncing, polling vs. interrupts.
software: Vendor IDE, Arduino IDE or PlatformIO

name: Digital Temperature Monitoring
summary: Read a temperature sensor and show the value on a serial console or a small display.
skills: ADC or a digital sensor bus
outcomes: Convert ADC counts to physical units

name: Basic Sensor Interfacing
summary: Connect a few common sensors and read them with the simplest suitable interface.
hardware: A light sensor, a distance sensor or similar
software: Vendor IDE, Arduino IDE or PlatformIO
outcomes: Read a datasheet for wiring and timing

name: ESP32 Wi-Fi Monitoring
summary: Publish sensor data over Wi-Fi and view it remotely.
software: An MQTT broker or HTTP endpoint

name: UART Communication
summary: Build a command interface over UART with a simple text protocol and a ring buffer.

name: I2C Sensor Integration
summary: Write a small driver for an I2C sensor, from reading the datasheet to returning calibrated values.
outcomes: Debug a bus with a logic analyzer

name: PWM Motor Control
summary: Drive a DC motor or servo with PWM and add simple speed feedback.
outcomes: Generate PWM at a chosen frequency and duty cycle
Separate logic and motor power safely
Try an open-loop vs. a feedback approach

name: FreeRTOS Task Scheduling
summary: Split an application into tasks that communicate with queues and semaphores.
hardware: A board supported by FreeRTOS (STM32, ESP32, ...)

name: Embedded Linux Device Driver
summary: Write and load a simple kernel module, then a driver for a real peripheral.
hardware: A Linux-capable board (e.g. a Raspberry Pi or BeagleBone class board)
A simple I2C / SPI / GPIO peripheral
software: Linux kernel headers or a kernel tree
outcomes: Build and load a kernel module
Expose a character device or sysfs entry
Describe hardware in a device tree

name: IoT Monitoring System
summary: End-to-end system: sensor nodes, a gateway or broker, storage and a dashboard, with secure updates.
software: A time-series store or simple database
outcomes: Design a data flow from node to dashboard

name: CAN Communication Project
summary: Make two or more nodes exchange messages over a CAN bus and decode them with analysis tools.
software: Vendor HAL or a CAN stack
outcomes: Understand IDs, arbitration and bit timing

name: Custom PCB-Based Embedded System
summary: Design, order, assemble and bring up a small board around a microcontroller.
hardware: A microcontroller with a datasheet and reference design
outcomes: Turn a reference design into a schematic and layout
Apply basic EMC and decoupling practice
Bring up and debug a first board

name: Edge AI on Microcontrollers
summary: Train a tiny model and run inference on a microcontroller using sensor data.
hardware: A microcontroller board with a suitable sensor (e.g. a motion or sound sensor)
software: A TinyML runtime (e.g. TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers)
